links.rationale: Both are closed-loop harness improvement with execute-evaluate-evolve structure.
NLAH externalizes harness logic as artifacts; AHE evolves file-level harness components—complementary views on harness as object.
AHE reports primary empirical gains on Terminal-Bench 2.
AHE observability surfaces align with VERO's structured traces and versioning for optimization science.
Comparable harness stacks (Harbor vs evolved coding harnesses) motivate cross-benchmark harness research.
Both stress retaining rich diagnostic history instead of lossy summaries for optimizers.
Meta-Harness evaluates discovered harnesses on TerminalBench-2.
Meta-Harness outer search parallels meta-level optimization of evolution blueprints.
Context collapse from monolithic rewriting parallels Meta-Harness critique of aggressively compressed optimizer feedback.
ACE evolves durable playbooks; IHR executes NL harness contracts—both treat non-weight artifacts as first-class adaptive state.
Pattern-layer framing connects to survey taxonomy of agent architectures and control.
Name collision: roadmap ACE is human command center; Zhang et al. ACE is context playbook engineering—both concern human-agent interfaces.
ACE paper evaluates on AppWorld leaderboard using the AppWorld simulator setting.
Survey discusses benchmarks; Terminal-Bench is a canonical terminal agent benchmark.
AppWorld stresses rich code + tool use; survey covers tool integration and evaluation for coding agents.
SE-for-agents modality implies tooling/observability gaps the survey raises for agent-compatible dev stacks.
Failure taxonomies inform what agent optimizers (VERO setting) must diagnose in target agents.
Structured merge/consultation packs echo VERO's emphasis on auditable artifacts and reproducible agent changes.
